Subject: Dedicated capacity ask: production throughput & latency targets

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. As discussed, Obsidian is evaluating a Dedicated deployment for our core inference path (customer-facing chat + summarization). We put together an initial requirements sheet (attached) but wanted a quick sanity check from Redwood on capacity sizing and whether our SLOs are realistic before we lock a commit. High level: 

- Workload: ~900k tokens/day baseline, projected to 2.2M tokens/day within 6 months (steady growth).
- Typical request: mix of chat and single-turn summarization. Median prompt ~160 tokens, median completion ~240 tokens => ~400 tokens per user request.
- Traffic shape: steady daytime plateau in EU (08:00–20:00 CET), with peak bursts 6–8x baseline lasting 10–30 minutes (events/marketing spikes).
- SLO target: p95 generation latency <= 600ms (end-to-end, client-observed).
- Availability: want predictable throughput for product launch; considering 6–12 month committed slab.

Can Redwood provide: estimated tokens/sec capacity required for those targets, recommended slab (GPU count & type), and suggested headroom / burst policy? We also want an explanation of fallback behavior if we hit a peak above committed slab.

Attachments: obsidian_req_v2.xlsx (workload sheet + sample logs).

Best,
Anya
Head of Platform
Obsidian Systems

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: production throughput & latency targets — sizing model

Quick sizing note (ballpark) based on Obsidian sheet and our p95 latency target. Assumptions up front:
- Model variant: open-llm-family-small-v2 (baseline). We expect ~0.8 tokens/ms on an A100-like GPU depending on quantization and batch packing.
- Typical request ~400 tokens (prompt+completion).
- Warmed KV cache for chat context where applicable (saves ~15–25% of compute on repeat patterns).
- Target p95 <= 600ms (client-observed generation time; excludes network egress).

Sizing math (conservative):
- Baseline tokens/day 900k => steady average tokens/sec = 900000 / 86400 ≈ 10.4 tps.
- 6-month projection 2.2M tokens/day => avg ≈ 25.5 tps.
- Translate tokens/sec to concurrent token throughput needed at p95: to keep p95 <=600ms for 400-token requests, we need per-request service time <=600ms. That implies throughput of at least ~1.66 requests/sec per model instance for single-request latency budget; but with batching we can push better token/s density.

Using our runtime perf profile:
- Single A100-class GPU (mixed precision, 8-bit quant) can sustain ~1,400–1,800 tokens/sec for interactive latencies with small batching. Use conservative 1,300 tps for headroom.
- Therefore a single GPU covers the projected spike request volume of ~25.5 tps easily in steady state. But spikes are the primary driver.

Peak burst planning:
- Observed bursts 6–8x baseline. If baseline avg tokens/sec (at 2.2M/day) ≈ 25.5 tps, 8x peak ⇒ ~204 tps.
- Required GPUs for peak (conservative): 204 / 1,300 ≈ 0.16 GPUs — that suggests compute is not the bottleneck for raw token TPS given the model choice. However p95 latency at burst depends on queueing, batching geometry, and GPU memory headroom.

Recommendations:
1) Commit slab: Start with a 2-GPU slab (A100-class or equivalent) for dedicated routing and isolation. 2 GPUs provide operational redundancy (one can be drained for maintenance) and give comfortable room for multi-tenant isolation within the customer slab (housekeeping processes, cache warming).
2) Burst policy: Enable elastic burst to shared capacity tier for short spikes (10–30m). Contractually specify a soft-burst allowance (e.g., up to 4x for 30 minutes) with automatic throttle to ensure p95 SLO protection.
3) Headroom: Target 25–35% compute headroom above expected 8x peak to cover queuing and inefficient packing during spikes. Practically, that means target capacity ~1.25x of modeled peak.
4) Latency levers: Recommend enabling prefix/KV cache for chat, use 8-bit quantization for lower memory footprint, and tune batching window to 40–80ms to reduce p95 under load.

Attachments: obsidian_sizing_model.csv (spreadsheet with per-minute token projections and GPU mapping).

If the customer wants a strictly guaranteed p95 with no burst fallback, we should size for sustained worst-case peak which will materially increase committed GPU count (I can run that run-rate calc if they prefer).

—Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: production throughput & latency targets — latency tail considerations

Adding a couple of latency-tail notes and operational recommendations: 

- Tail latencies often balloon during cold cache misses and when model variants/quant levels differ. Recommend a small warm pool of 1–2 pre-warmed replicas per slab to minimize cold-start tail spikes for scheduled events.
- For p95 <= 600ms, prioritize small batching windows (<=60ms) in the serving runtime. That trades a little throughput efficiency for predictable p95.
- Quantization: moving to 8-bit (we recommend our tested q8 pathway) keeps performance within the conservative 1,300 tps per A100 assumption; q4f16 can reduce memory and allow larger packing but may increase per-token latency variance.
- Canary & rollback: add a canary route for heavy traffic flows. If latency regression >15% at p95, auto-fallback to a slightly smaller model variant with guaranteed lower inference latency. Document this in the SLA as an acceptable graceful degradation path.

Finally: confirm whether Obsidian expects the SLO to include network transit and their client-side rendering. If yes, we should budget an additional ~50–120ms in the p95 compute budget.

Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask: production throughput & latency targets — proposal & next steps

Anya — thanks for the clear ask and for the sample logs. Summary of our proposal and next steps below.

What we recommend (short answer):
- Start with a 2 x A100-class GPU Dedicated slab for the initial committed period (6 months).
- Modeled conservative capability: ~2,600 tokens/sec aggregate (2 GPUs @ ~1,300 tps each) with production tuning. That maps to headroom ~1.25x on an 8x peak scenario from your 6-month projection.
- Expected p95 generation latency: ~350–500ms with prefix caching and 8-bit quantization under modeled spike patterns. We will reserve ~75–120ms for network/client budget if you want an end-to-end p95 promise.
- Burst policy: soft burst to shared pool up to 4x for 30 minutes (automated), with contractual option to increase committed slab for guaranteed hard SLOs.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- If you require hard guarantees with no fallback throttling, we must size for sustained worst-case peak which increases cost significantly.
- Tail latency during large simultaneous cold-cache events may exceed p95 targets unless pre-warm replicas are included.

Next steps:
1) Anya — confirm whether Obsidian is OK with a soft-burst policy (soft bursts to shared capacity with automatic throttling) or whether you require hard commitments.
2) If soft-burst is OK, we'll prepare a commercial proposal (DEAL-7831) for 2 GPUs with a recommended burst addendum and canary rollback policy.
3) We'll share a short one-pager (pdf) summarizing perf assumptions and an itemized pricing appendix.

Linking docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ObsidianSizing and HubSpot HS-1234567. Attached: obsidian_proposal_summary.pdf
